title: Certified Verification of NEXPTIME-Hardness for Degree-Bounded Local-Sum MPNN Satisfiability
abstract: Marco Salzer (arXiv:2611.32595, Nov 2026) proved that degree-bounded satisfiability (DEGBSAT) for local-sum Message Passing Neural Networks with ReLU activations and rational node labels is NEXPTIME-hard even at fixed degree bound d = 3, closing the PSPACE-vs-NEXP gap via a proof architecture proposed by GPT-6 Astra. We present a standalone zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization of 18 core rational-encoding, polyhedral-count, ReLU-FNN, and MPNN acceptance theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero Classical.choice) paired with an exact-Q four-mode certificate verifier (MPNN-DEGBSAT-CERT-1.0) that executes Salzer's full (h+2)-layer MPNN M_w without floating-point arithmetic. Across 16 canonical certificates (0.080-114.497 ms, total 286.40 ms), all invariants replay identically over Q while rejecting 62/62 live adversarial forgery attacks.
ai_assistance_disclosure: Prepared by sole author Lluis Eriksson with AI coding, formalization, and drafting assistance from Google Antigravity; all Lean 4.35.0 proofs, exact-Q certificates, and adversarial tests were independently compiled and machine-verified locally.

target_reference.title: Degree-bounded Satisfiability of Local MPNNs with Sum Aggregation is NEXPTIME-hard
